notes: Perfect match (Jaccard=1.0) on all 10 claims about the in vitro extract system recapitulating spindle size differences. Both agree this work is profound and well-supported.

Perfect match (Jaccard=1.0) on all 7 claims about developmental transition in spindle assembly pathways from chromatin-mediated to centrosome-dominated. Both consider this part of the profound first section.

Perfect match (Jaccard=1.0) on all 7 claims about kif2a as driver of spindle scaling. Both accept kif2a's role through antibody inhibition experiments, though peer reviewers want more mechanistic detail about importin α regulation.

High overlap (Jaccard=0.857) on 6 shared claims about MT dynamics measurements showing increased catastrophe frequency. Both accept these quantitative data as part of the strong extract characterization work. LLM includes C65 not in peer review.
Good overlap (Jaccard=0.636) on 7 shared claims about in vivo microinjection experiments showing kif2a effects on spindle size and orientation. Both accept these functional observations as valid.

Limited overlap (Jaccard=0.2) on 2 shared claims (C7, C8) about functional consequences of altered spindle size. Both accept that impaired orientation but robust chromosome segregation occur when spindle size is manipulated.

Moderate overlap (Jaccard=0.409) on 9 shared claims about importin α redistribution and functional consequences. LLM finds evidence sufficient for importin α membrane partitioning mechanism, but peer reviewers state data 'not strong enough' and request more direct quantitative measurements (FCS, FRET, quantitative pull-downs).

Moderate overlap (Jaccard=0.318) on 7 shared claims about reciprocal perturbation experiments with kif2a and importin α. LLM considers the kif2a:importin α ratio mechanism well-supported, but peer reviewers find mechanistic insights insufficient and want more direct evidence.

Good overlap (Jaccard=0.667) on 4 shared claims about the complete ratiometric mechanism. LLM finds the overall mechanism well-supported, but peer reviewers indicate the mechanistic data are 'not strong enough' requiring more quantitative evidence for importin α redistribution.

Low overlap (Jaccard=0.12) on 3 shared claims (C5, C83, C85) about importin α binding and inhibition of kif2a. LLM finds biochemical evidence (co-IP, in vitro inhibition) sufficient, but peer reviewers want more direct mechanistic evidence as part of broader concerns about the importin α mechanism.

Minimal overlap (Jaccard=0.167) on 1 shared claim (C110) about whether MT destabilization fully accounts for spindle scaling. Both express uncertainty about completeness of the mechanistic understanding, with LLM noting authors' acknowledgment of gaps and peer reviewers wanting stronger mechanistic insights.

Minimal overlap (Jaccard=0.038) on 1 shared claim (C112). LLM R10 addresses complete mechanism (C9, C109, C112, C114, C115) finding it supported, while peer R5 addresses broader importin α mechanism (22 claims) with uncertainty. The single shared claim about cell-autonomous function is insufficient for full comparison.

LLM evaluates 4 claims (C54, C56, C57, C58) about extract mixing and nuclei depletion experiments demonstrating cytoplasmic control. No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific claims, though they relate to the accepted first part of the paper.

LLM evaluates 2 claims (C110, C116) about whether MT destabilization mechanisms fully account for spindle scaling. Only C110 appears in peer review (matched above); C116 about generality across mechanisms is unique to LLM evaluation.
LLM evaluates 1 claim (C128) about whether multiple importin α bands represent phosphorylation or other modifications. No corresponding peer review result addresses this specific mechanistic gap.
LLM evaluates 4 claims (C147, C148, C149, C150) about the mechanism maintaining metaphase orientation. No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific mechanistic speculations.

LLM evaluates 3 claims (C50, C51, C52) about chromosome misalignment defects in extracts and limitations of the system. No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific observations about extract limitations.

LLM evaluates 2 claims (C136, C138) about whether importin α limits kif2a in egg extracts and cultured cells. No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific questions about mechanism generality.
